activation_pct_note: From the Spera et al. anneal series (companion papers S1/S2 describe the same samples).

Middle anneal temperature as printed in the S2 abstract (1675, 1175 and 1825 C); 1175 C may be a typographical error for 1775 C. Activation at this point is not reported in the accessible text and is left as NA.
From the Spera et al. anneal series (companion papers S1/S2 describe the same samples).
Derived: hole concentration (8.9e19 cm-3) divided by implanted concentration (1.5e21 cm-3, from dose and an assumed 0.2 um box depth). Not stated in the paper.
Derived: hole concentration (~3.0e19 cm-3) divided by implanted concentration (1.5e21 cm-3). Same batch as the 1 min row; longer anneal.

Derived: hole concentration (5.7e19 cm-3) divided by implanted concentration (1.5e21 cm-3). Orientation (11-20 vs 0001), room-temperature implantation and C co-implantation all differ from the 0001 rows, so the orientation effect cannot be isolated.

Net effective activation, 100% minus the compensation fraction (84% at ~9e16 cm-3). Different definition from the Hall-fit rows; not pooled with the Hall-fit rows. Superseded by the two-defect-model rows from the AIP Advances paper (rows 33-34).
Net effective activation, 100% minus the compensation fraction (27% at ~2e19 cm-3). Same definitional caveat as row 7; the samples may overlap with the AIP Advances 2019 companion paper.
Al concentration 8e20 cm-3 (highest of the 5e19-8e20 range); minimum resistivity 2e-2 Ohm cm.
Lower fluence, no cap. Scanning capacitance microscopy, not Hall effect.
Higher fluence, no cap. Scanning capacitance microscopy, not Hall effect.
Lower fluence, graphite cap. Scanning capacitance microscopy, not Hall effect. Same fluence as row 10, giving a within-study capping comparison.
Higher fluence, graphite cap. Scanning capacitance microscopy, not Hall effect. Same fluence as row 11, giving a within-study capping comparison.

Activation ratio >70% (normalized to the SIMS Mg concentration). Acceptor concentration (2.6 +/- 0.8)e18 cm-3 and ionization energy 212 +/- 5 meV from a temperature-dependent Hall fit (275-500 K) rather than a single-temperature r_H = 1 assumption.
Lowest-temperature point (1573 K) of the isochronal series.
Highest-temperature point (1753 K) of the isochronal series; reported as almost 100% with a compensation ratio of 12%.
Acceptor density divided by Mg density (2e19 cm-3). Anneal temperature and time for this value are not given in the accessible text.
Original multicycle-RTA demonstration. Anneal conditions for this value are not given in the accessible text.
Na/[Mg] ~70% with sequential N co-implantation; compensating-donor ratio Nd/Na ~18%. The Mg-only comparison in the same paper is not entered as a separate row.
Acceptor concentration equal to the implanted Mg concentration (~100% nominal) with a carbon cap during UHPA; compensation ratio 9%.

Room-temperature implant. Qualitative entry: heavy compensation and no p-type conduction at low diffusion budget despite structural damage recovery. Quantitative conditions from the paper's Table I are rows 64-67.

Derived from Table I of the source: activation = sheet hole concentration / implant dose (1.4e14 cm-2). Room-temperature implant. One of four (anneal temperature, anneal time) conditions from the same table (rows 64-67).
Derived from Table I, same method as row 64; replaces the abstract's 'almost 100%' with a tabulated value.
Derived from Table I, same method as row 64. Lower temperature (1200 C) with longer time (100 min) gives higher activation than row 64 (1300 C, 10 min, 46.4%).
Derived from Table I, same method as row 64. Fixed-temperature (1300 C) time series with row 64: 10 min gives 46.4%, 100 min gives 71.4%.

No free holes observed for 1300 C UHPA samples (Hall measurement not possible), in apparent conflict with the 23% activation reported by Hirukawa et al. at the same nominal condition. Possible causes (pressure, Mg concentration, sample differences) are not resolved. Activation is entered as 0 to denote no detectable free holes, not a measured zero.

Target concentration 1.8e20 Al cm-3. Activation as adjusted in the paper, assuming 100% as the maximum; resistivity 1.56 Ohm cm. Part of a 2 x 4 (implant temperature x anneal temperature) factorial design, 8 rows in total.
Resistivity 0.59 Ohm cm. Same factorial design as row 23.
Resistivity 0.40 Ohm cm. Same factorial design as row 23.
Resistivity 0.29 Ohm cm. Same factorial design as row 23. Tabulated values (5.6/16/25/36%) are used instead of the rounded range quoted in the abstract.
Resistivity 0.32 Ohm cm; mobility 5.6-8.4 cm2/Vs, lower than for the 650 C implants and attributed by the authors to compensating defects. Same factorial design, higher implant-temperature arm.
Resistivity 0.23 Ohm cm.
Resistivity 0.20 Ohm cm, the best value quoted in the abstract.
Resistivity 0.18 Ohm cm, the table minimum (the abstract rounds to ~0.20 Ohm cm).

Concentration-dependence endpoint (3.33e18 cm-3): activation ratio ~0.5 falling to ~0.25 at 1e21 cm-3. Anneal temperature and time not available from the accessible text; not used in anneal-temperature analyses.
Concentration-dependence endpoint (1e21 cm-3). Same caveat as row 31.
Preferred two-defect model, sample A (target Al 1e17 cm-3). Compensation ratio 39% (Table I), so net activation = 100% - 39% = 61%. Deep acceptor level ~400 meV. Supersedes rows 7-8.
Preferred two-defect model, sample B (target Al 1e18 cm-3). Compensation ratio 33% (Table I), so net activation = 67%. Deep acceptor level ~280 meV. Supersedes rows 7-8.

Acceptor activation ratio of 80% with no dependence on anneal time from 1 s to 30 min for anneal temperatures between 1700 and 1900 C. A single anneal temperature/time pair cannot be assigned from the abstract; recorded as a range.

Maximum activation of 80% for room-temperature B implantation and a 1150 C anneal; concentration 3.6e19 cm-3, shallow box profile ~130 nm; hole concentration >1e14 cm-3, mobility >110 cm2/Vs. A 1300 C anneal was also tested; its activation is not given in the abstract and is not entered.
Room-temperature implantation, furnace anneal up to 1650 C; activation of up to 30% of implanted boron. 2 MeV implantation, a different energy regime from the other diamond rows.

Compensation ratio 0.05 and hole mobility 385 cm2/Vs. Thermal history: -97 C implantation, in-situ heating to 1050 C (10 min), then furnace anneal at 1450 C (10 min); the anneal temperature given is not the full process. Activation left NA because the compensation ratio is not 1 - activation.
Qualitative entry. Room-temperature implantation at 3.5e20 cm-3 graphitizes the implanted layer (resistivity ~1e-3 Ohm cm). No activation percentage is given.

Qualitative entry. Implantation at 400 C (and 800 C) at the same or higher dose (up to 3.5e21 cm-3) preserves the diamond Raman peak at 1332 cm-1 with low resistivity (~1e-3 Ohm cm) and no graphitization. No activation percentage is given.

Qualitative time series: room-temperature implant, 1300 C anneal, 5-240 min. The ionization energy approaches the theoretical 0.3 eV only with increasing time; anneals of 120 min or less leave deep levels. No activation percentage is given.
Maximum activation over the dose range 9.2e13-2.3e15 cm-2; reported as the highest value for conventional RTA (not UHPA).
Derived, low confidence: hole concentration (1.23e15 cm-3) / implanted concentration (~1e19 cm-3, abstract-level precision) = 0.0123%. Gyrotron microwave anneal.
Reported as perfect doping efficiency over 2e17-2e19 cm-3; room-temperature implant, CVD homoepitaxial film. No numeric value beyond 'perfect'; entered as 100%.
High-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) anneal, reported as ten times more efficient than vacuum annealing at this temperature. Implant temperature not stated in the abstract; room temperature assumed.
Lowest implanted concentration (1e19 cm-3) of a 1e19-8e20 cm-3 range; 1950 C, 5 min. Neutrality-equation fit: 73% activation, 31% compensation, 146 meV ionization level.

Doping efficiency of ~50% after a 1600 C anneal (following a 1450 C step), reported as the highest for B-implanted diamond at the time. Two samples (5e18 and 5e19 cm-3) were tested; the abstract does not identify which one gives the 50%.

90-100% activation (midpoint used) at 900 C for Be concentration below 5e18 cm-3. A separate activation maximum near 700 C occurs at higher fluences (not entered). Implant temperature not stated; room temperature assumed.
Shallow (40 nm) Be implant, RTA, peak concentration 3e19 cm-3. Anneal temperature not stated in the abstract.
RTA with halogen lamps. Measured at 77 K, not room temperature. Anneal temperature not stated in the abstract.
Same paper, higher dose. Measured at 77 K. Anneal temperature not stated in the abstract.
Maximum electrical activation of Be reached at 550 C. No numeric activation is given in the abstract and none is entered.
Preamorphized (As implant at liquid-nitrogen temperature) Be implant with RTA; complete activation per the abstract (entered as 100%, qualitative). Anneal temperature not stated in the abstract.

Anneal temperatures >=700 C are required for maximum activation, and >=50% is generally achievable. Multi-energy implant (up to 400 keV), room temperature, as-implanted concentration ~3e18 cm-3. Entered as a lower bound.
Low-power pulsed-laser anneal in N2 (not a furnace anneal). Hole concentration profile matches the implanted Zn profile, i.e. ~100% where [Zn] plateaus. No anneal temperature applicable.
Mg-only implant (room temperature), dose 1e15 cm-2; compared with row 57 from the same batch. Peak hole concentration 5.4e18 cm-3. RTA temperature not stated in the abstract.
Mg + P dual implant, same dose and batch as row 56: P co-implantation raises activation from 40% to 68%. Peak hole concentration 1.1e19 cm-3.
Si, used as a contrast system. For crystalline Si below 1000 C, activation proceeds slowly and is not completed on RTA timescales. No single percentage at 950 C is given in the abstract.
For T >= 1000 C complete activation is obtained in about 10 s in crystalline Si. Preamorphized Si activates quickly at all temperatures examined (not entered as a separate row).
BF2+ into amorphized Si. Sheet resistance of 85 Ohm/sq after RTA (1250 C, 10-15 s) is close to that expected for 100% activation at 2e15 cm-2. At the higher dose (row 61) this no longer holds.
Derived: same conditions as row 60 at 6e15 cm-2. Peak carrier concentration ~1e20 cm-3 against an as-implanted ~1e21 cm-3 gives ~10%; the percentage is not stated in the paper.
Complete damage annealing with full electrical activation for shallow implants after RTA (qualitative, entered as 100%). No temperature given in the abstract.

Silicon-on-insulator substrate, isochronal furnace anneals at 450-1050 C for 30 min. Significantly less activation below 750 C; between 750 and 900 C the active dose is similar to bulk Si. No percentage is given for this point.
